question.problem: Find the surface area of the portion of the plane $z=3y-\sqrt{6}x$ whose projection onto the $xy$-plane is bounded by $y={x}^{3},$ $y=1,$ and the $y$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $z=f(x,y)$ with $(x,y)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

In this case, our surface is given by

$$
z=3y-\sqrt{6}x,\,(x,y)\in D
$$

where the region $D$ is given by

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,{x}^{3}\le y\le 1\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14221663/assets/9f6192b3c3c61fc0abfd6c4ec46d127431265c870bc38d7deac79353b6923fdd.png)

Now, since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂z}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3y-\sqrt{6}x)=-\sqrt{6}, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3y-\sqrt{6}x)=3,\end{aligned}
$$

the surface area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(-\sqrt{6})}^{2}+(3)^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{16}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{3}}^{1}4\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4\cdot y\,{|}_{{x}^{3}}^{1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4-4{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(4x-{x}^{4}){|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(4-1)-0 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
